questions: Does the wider ±0.04 m span with 16 mm footprints keep the sum of readings above 0.05 at the point where the robot previously lost the line? If not, on which track and at which bend?
Is the step at which the first line loss begins the same on every track? If it is at the start, the cause is the initial pose and not the bends.
With yaw inertia reduced to about 0.5 kg-scale, does the robot now oscillate or overshoot on the slalom, or does steering_oscillation stay near 0.13 to 0.15?
Does the sensor array now saturate near the centre (all readings near 1), which would reduce the signal's resolution at small errors?

intent: Test whether lateral sensor coverage is the cause of the single line loss that starts each failure. The sensor span widens from ±0.03 m to ±0.04 m, with 16 mm footprints so the array sees tape out to about ±0.06 m from the centre line. The iteration 0 wheel_track of 0.12 m is restored, since the narrower track did not help the oval. Mass and body length drop to 0.5 kg and 0.12 m to cut yaw inertia. Expected: line_loss_events fall toward 0, max_error stays below 0.06 m for longer, and progress on the s-bend and slalom rises above the iteration 0 values (0.14 and 0.10).
learning: Iterations 0 and 1 show that the failure is a single line loss followed by drift off the track. Max error sits just above 0.06 m in both. Changing wheel_track alone did not help, so the next test isolates sensor coverage (span and footprint) on the same drivetrain. If line losses disappear and max_error still reaches the limit, the drivetrain or controller gain is the bottleneck.
rationale: Evidence across iterations 0 and 1 (both 0 of 60 completions) shows the same failure. Max error reaches 0.062 to 0.066 m, just past the 0.06 m off-track limit, and line_loss_events sit at about 1.0 per run on the s-bend and slalom. Progress is low (0.10 to 0.23). The robot loses the tape once and then drifts off before covering the course. Iteration 1 scored worse than iteration 0 (53.7 vs 63.0) after I changed wheel_track to 0.10 m, lowered mass and body length, moved the sensors forward and widened the footprint to 16 mm. Those changes did not help, and because I changed five things at once I cannot attribute the drop to any one of them. Two findings look solid. First, the off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), which is 0.06 m across the whole body_width range, so body width cannot help. Second, a single line loss is what starts the failure, which points at sensor coverage at the edge of the tape band. The sensor span of 0.06 m (about ±0.03 m) with 16 mm footprints only sees tape out to roughly ±0.05 m from the centre line. A robot that drifts to 0.055 m or more can therefore lose the tape completely. This iteration I keep the iteration 0 drivetrain (wheel_track 0.12 m, since the narrower track did not improve the oval) and make two targeted changes. I widen the sensor span to ±0.04 m (x = ±0.04, ±0.02, 0) so the array still sees tape at larger lateral error, and I keep 16 mm footprints for that same coverage. I also reduce mass to 0.5 kg and body_length to 0.12 m to lower yaw inertia, which the Integrator's feedback suggested as the next lever. The sensors stay at y = 0.06 m. Expected result: line_loss_events drop toward 0 on the s-bend and slalom, max_error stays under 0.06 m for longer, and progress rises. This will show whether coverage or turn authority is the limit. If max_error still reaches 0.06 m with line losses at 0, the drivetrain is the bottleneck and I will move to a narrower wheel_track next.
